title: Annotatio III §.XI (8): Nomenclature — ‘Transsubstantiation’ misfits; nearer annihilation of one substance and creation of another
pass_a_gloss: Finally (8.) by its own Nomenclature, by which it wishes to be called Transsubstantiation i.e. Conversion of Substance into substance — which Conversion nonetheless by no means obtains, it being supposed that through the same nothing remains from bread and wine — so that under that name it rather deserves to be called Annihilation of one substance and Creation of another, than Transsubstantiation.
pass_b_english: (8) By its own name: it wants ‘Transsubstantiation’ = conversion of substance into substance.
But if nothing of bread and wine remains, the truer name is annihilation of one substance and creation of another — not Transsubstantiation.
source_text: Denique (8.) Sui ipsius Nomenclaturæ, quâ Transsubstantiatio dici cupit i. e. Conversio Substantiæ in substantiam, qualis tamen Conversio neutiquam obtinet, suppositô, ex pane & vino per eandem nihil remanere, ut rectius eô nomine Annihilatio substantiæ unius, & alterius substantiæ Creatio, quam Transsubstantiatio, dici mereatur.
